# Reservation Management Device for Battery Pack Exchange Systems

## Overview

The reservation management device (50) constitutes a specialized system designed to coordinate and manage reservations for battery pack (10) exchanges occurring at a designated charging device (30). This device serves as the central control mechanism that governs the scheduling and availability determination process for battery exchange operations, ensuring that the exchange process at the charging device operates efficiently and without conflicts between multiple reservation requests.

## Core Functional Components

### Reservation Number Acquisition Component (53)

The reservation management device (50) incorporates a reservation number acquisition component (53), which is specifically configured to acquire data pertaining to the number of battery packs (10) that have been reserved, or are intended to be reserved, for exchange at the charging device (30). This component functions as the primary data-gathering mechanism for tracking incoming demand for battery packs at the charging station, effectively monitoring how many units are anticipated to be withdrawn or exchanged based on existing or pending reservations.

### Return Number Acquisition Component (54)

Complementing the reservation number acquisition component, the device (50) further includes a return number acquisition component (54). This component is tasked with acquiring data representing the number of battery packs (10) that are scheduled or expected to be returned to the charging device (30). By tracking the anticipated influx of battery packs back into the charging station's inventory, this component provides essential information regarding the supply side of the battery exchange equation, complementing the demand-side data gathered by the reservation number acquisition component.

### Reservation Possibility Determination Component (55)

The reservation management device (50) additionally comprises a reservation possibility determination component (55), which serves as the decision-making core of the system. This component is responsible for determining whether a new battery pack (10) exchange reservation can be accommodated at the charging device (30) at a given point in time or for a specified future period.

## Integrated Determination Logic

The reservation possibility determination component (55) performs its evaluative function by combining and cross-referencing the data acquired from both the reservation number acquisition component (53) and the return number acquisition component (54). Specifically, the component synthesizes the number of battery packs (10) that have already been reserved for exchange (as tracked by component 53) with the number of battery packs (10) that are expected to be returned to the charging device (30) within the relevant timeframe (as tracked by component 54).

Through this combined analysis, the reservation possibility determination component (55) is able to calculate the effective availability of battery packs (10) at the charging device (30), taking into account both the depleting effect of existing reservations and the replenishing effect of anticipated returns. This integrated approach enables the device (50) to make accurate, real-time determinations regarding whether sufficient battery pack inventory will be available to fulfill new reservation requests, thereby preventing overbooking scenarios and ensuring that the charging device (30) can reliably meet the exchange needs of its users while maintaining optimal inventory management throughout the reservation lifecycle.

# Reservation Management Device for Battery Pack Exchange Systems

## Background and Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a reservation management device (50) designed to facilitate and optimize the reservation process for battery pack (10) exchange operations at charging devices (30). As electric vehicles and other battery-powered systems become increasingly prevalent, the demand for efficient battery exchange infrastructure has grown substantially. Charging stations equipped with battery exchange capabilities must effectively manage the availability of charged battery packs to serve users who wish to reserve exchange slots in advance, while simultaneously accounting for battery packs that are scheduled to be returned to the station's inventory.

## Detailed Description of the Invention

The reservation management device (50) comprises several interconnected functional components that work in concert to provide accurate, real-time assessment of battery exchange availability.

### Reservation Number Acquisition Component

The reservation number acquisition component (53) is configured to collect and process data pertaining to the number of battery packs that have been reserved or are in the process of being reserved for exchange by users. This component continuously monitors incoming reservation requests, tracking the quantity of battery packs that prospective users intend to withdraw from the charging device at specified future times. By maintaining an accurate count of pending reservations, this component establishes a critical data point for determining the outbound demand on the charging station's battery inventory.

### Return Number Acquisition Component

Complementing the reservation number acquisition component, the return number acquisition component (54) is tasked with gathering data related to battery packs that are anticipated to be returned to the charging device within a relevant timeframe. This component tracks battery packs currently in use by customers that are scheduled or expected to be brought back to the station, whether through pre-arranged return commitments or predictive modeling based on usage patterns. The return number data provides essential insight into the inbound supply of battery packs that will become available for future exchanges.

### Reservation Possibility Determination Component

The reservation possibility determination component (55) serves as the central decision-making element of the device, synthesizing the data acquired by both the reservation number acquisition component and the return number acquisition component. By integrating these two data streams, this component calculates the net availability of battery packs at any given point in time, accounting for both the depletion of inventory due to reserved exchanges and the replenishment of inventory due to expected returns.

Through this combined analysis, the reservation possibility determination component is able to accurately assess whether a new reservation request for battery pack exchange can be accommodated without exceeding the physical or logistical capacity of the charging device. This determination takes into consideration the temporal dynamics of battery pack availability, ensuring that the system does not merely rely on static, current-moment inventory counts but rather incorporates forward-looking projections based on both scheduled reservations and anticipated returns.

## Advantages of the Invention

The integration of the reservation number acquisition component and the return number acquisition component within a single reservation possibility determination component provides several significant advantages over conventional battery exchange management systems:

1. **Enhanced Accuracy**: By considering both outgoing reservations and incoming returns, the device provides a more precise picture of battery pack availability than systems that consider only one of these factors in isolation.

2. **Improved Efficiency**: The charging device operator can optimize the utilization of available battery packs, reducing instances of both overbooking (where reservations exceed actual availability) and underutilization (where available battery packs go unused due to overly conservative reservation policies).

3. **Better User Experience**: Users seeking to reserve battery pack exchanges receive more reliable confirmations, as the reservation possibility determination component accounts for the dynamic nature of battery pack inventory throughout the day.

4. **Scalability**: The modular architecture of the reservation management device, with distinct components for reservation tracking, return tracking, and possibility determination, allows for straightforward adaptation to charging stations of varying sizes and battery pack throughput volumes.

5. **Reduced Operational Disruptions**: By accurately forecasting battery pack availability, charging station operators can better manage staffing, inventory logistics, and customer communications, minimizing disruptions caused by inaccurate availability predictions.

## Conclusion

The reservation management device (50) represents a significant advancement in the management of battery pack exchange operations at charging devices (30). Through the coordinated function of the reservation number acquisition component (53), the return number acquisition component (54), and the reservation possibility determination component (55), the invention enables charging station operators to maintain a dynamic, accurate, and efficient system for managing battery exchange reservations, ultimately improving service reliability and customer satisfaction while optimizing the utilization of available battery pack resources.

# The Word "The"

"The" is perhaps the most unassuming yet powerful word in the English language. As the definite article, it performs a quiet but essential function: transforming the abstract into the specific, the general into the particular.

Consider the difference between "a book" and "the book." The former could be any book, floating in a sea of possibilities. The latter points to something specific—a book both speaker and listener understand, whether through prior context, physical presence, or shared knowledge. This tiny shift in specificity is the entire job of "the."

Linguistically, "the" is remarkably humble. It carries no inherent meaning of its own—no color, no emotion, no concrete image. Yet it appears more frequently than any other word in written and spoken English. Studies of word frequency consistently place "the" at the very top of the list, appearing millions of times more often than words we might consider more "important" or meaningful.

Despite its ubiquity, "the" poses genuine challenges for language learners. Many languages don't have definite articles at all (like Russian or Japanese), while others use them in ways that don't map neatly onto English patterns. Deciding when to use "the," when to use "a" or "an," and when to use no article at all requires an intuitive grasp of context that often takes years to develop.

"The" also plays a fascinating role in titles and names, lending gravity and definiteness. "The Beatles" suggests a singular, defined entity—there is only one band that gets to claim that particular "the." Similarly, phrases like "the end" or "the beginning" carry a sense of finality or singular importance that indefinite versions would lack.

In essence, "the" is a linguistic pointer, a tool for shared understanding. It's a word so small it often escapes notice, yet so essential that language would lose precision and clarity without it. Its power lies not in what it says, but in what it assumes—shared context, mutual understanding, and the simple act of pointing to something and saying, "this one, specifically."

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF INVENTION
RESERVATION MANAGEMENT DEVICE, RESERVATION MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, AND RESERVATION MANAGEMENT METHOD FOR BATTERY EXCHANGE STATION

---

## TECHNICAL FIELD

The present invention relates to a reservation management device, a reservation management system, and a reservation management method for managing reservations of charged batteries at a battery exchange station used for electric vehicles (EVs), electric motorcycles, and other electrically-driven mobile bodies. More particularly, the present invention relates to a technique for determining whether a new reservation for battery exchange can be accepted, based on a comparison between the number of batteries already reserved and the number of batteries expected to be returned to the station.

---

## BACKGROUND ART

In recent years, battery exchange stations have been proposed as an alternative to conventional plug-in charging for electric vehicles. At a battery exchange station, a user removes a depleted battery from a vehicle and receives a charged battery stored at the station, thereby avoiding the long waiting times associated with direct charging.

Since the number of charged batteries stored at a battery exchange station at any given time is finite, it is desirable to allow users to reserve a charged battery in advance of their arrival, so as to guarantee availability. However, if reservations are accepted without regard to the actual number of charged batteries that will be available at the station, a situation may arise in which a user arrives at the station in accordance with a confirmed reservation, only to find that no charged battery is available for exchange. This is because, in addition to newly charged batteries, the pool of available batteries is also replenished by depleted batteries returned by other users, which must be charged before they can be dispensed; and the number of such returned batteries fluctuates dynamically and is difficult to predict with certainty at the time a reservation request is received.

Conventional reservation management systems generally determine reservation availability solely based on a fixed number of batteries physically present and fully charged at the station at the time of the reservation request. Such systems fail to account for batteries that are expected to be returned to the station, and become available after charging, within the reservation period. As a result, conventional systems tend to unnecessarily restrict the number of reservations that can be accepted, thereby lowering convenience for users, or, conversely, fail to accurately predict shortages, resulting in a discrepancy between reserved and actual available battery counts.

Accordingly, there is a need for a reservation management device capable of appropriately determining reservation availability by taking into account both the number of batteries already reserved by other users and the number of batteries expected to be returned to the station within a relevant time period.

---

## SUMMARY OF INVENTION

### Problem to be Solved by the Invention

An object of the present invention is to provide a reservation management device, a reservation management system, and a reservation management method capable of appropriately determining, at the time a reservation request is received, whether or not a new reservation for a charged battery at a battery exchange station can be accepted, by comparing the number of batteries already reserved against the number of batteries expected to be returned to the station, thereby improving the accuracy of reservation availability determination and preventing a shortage of charged batteries at the time of a user's visit.

### Means for Solving the Problem

In order to solve the above problem, a reservation management device according to one aspect of the present invention includes:

an acquisition unit configured to acquire reservation information indicating a number of reserved batteries that have been reserved by users for exchange at a battery exchange station within a predetermined period, and return information indicating a number of returned batteries that are expected to be returned to the battery exchange station within the predetermined period;

a comparison unit configured to compare the number of reserved batteries with the number of returned batteries; and

a determination unit configured to determine whether a new reservation request is to be accepted, based on a result of the comparison performed by the comparison unit.

In one embodiment, the determination unit is configured to determine that the new reservation request can be accepted when the number of returned batteries is equal to or greater than the number of reserved batteries plus a number of batteries requested in the new reservation request, and to determine that the new reservation request cannot be accepted, or that the new reservation request is to be accepted subject to a condition, when the number of returned batteries is less than said sum.

In another embodiment, the reservation management device further includes a battery stock acquisition unit configured to acquire a current stock number indicating a number of charged batteries currently available at the battery exchange station, wherein the determination unit determines whether the new reservation request can be accepted based on the current stock number, the number of reserved batteries, and the number of returned batteries.

In still another embodiment, the return information is generated based on at least one of: a scheduled return time reported in advance by a user, a statistical return pattern derived from historical data corresponding to a day of the week and a time zone, and a remaining charge level of a battery mounted on a vehicle of a user who is expected to visit the station within the predetermined period, obtained via communication with the vehicle or a terminal of the user.

The reservation management device may further include a notification unit configured to notify a terminal of a user having transmitted the new reservation request of a result of the determination made by the determination unit, and, when the new reservation request cannot be accepted, to notify the terminal of at least one of: another available time slot, another battery exchange station having an available charged battery, and a waiting list registration option.

### Effects of the Invention

According to the present invention, since whether or not to accept a new reservation is determined based on a comparison between the number of batteries already reserved and the number of batteries expected to be returned within a predetermined period, it is possible to accurately reflect the actual availability of charged batteries at the battery exchange station, including batteries that are not yet charged but are scheduled to be returned and recharged. This makes it possible to prevent a situation in which a user with a confirmed reservation arrives at the station and no charged battery is available, while also avoiding unnecessary restriction of reservation acceptance, thereby improving both the reliability of the reservation system and the convenience for users.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** is a block diagram showing an overall configuration of a reservation management system according to an embodiment of the present invention.

**FIG. 2** is a block diagram showing a functional configuration of a reservation management device according to an embodiment of the present invention.

**FIG. 3** is a diagram illustrating an example of reservation information and return information managed by the reservation management device.

**FIG. 4** is a flowchart showing a procedure of a reservation management method according to an embodiment of the present invention.

**FIG. 5** is a diagram illustrating an example of a screen displayed on a user terminal indicating a result of a reservation determination.

**FIG. 6** is a diagram illustrating a modification in which a current battery stock number is additionally used in the determination.

---

## DESCRIPTION OF EMBODIMENTS

### 1. Overall System Configuration

FIG. 1 shows a reservation management system 1 according to an embodiment of the present invention. The reservation management system 1 includes a reservation management device 10, one or more battery exchange stations 20 (20a, 20b, ..., 20n), one or more user terminals 30, and a network 40 connecting these components communicably with one another.

Each battery exchange station 20 is provided with a plurality of battery storage slots 21 in which batteries 22 are stored, a charging unit 23 configured to charge batteries 22 stored in the storage slots 21, a station control unit 24 configured to control the exchange of batteries with vehicles and to detect a state of each battery 22 (for example, whether it is charged, being charged, or newly returned and depleted), and a communication unit 25 configured to communicate with the reservation management device 10 via the network 40.

The user terminal 30 is, for example, a smartphone, a car navigation device, or an onboard unit mounted on a vehicle, and is configured to transmit a reservation request to the reservation management device 10 and to receive a result of a reservation determination therefrom.

### 2. Configuration of Reservation Management Device

FIG. 2 shows a functional configuration of the reservation management device 10. The reservation management device 10 includes a communication interface 11, a control unit 12, and a storage unit 13.

The control unit 12 includes, as functional blocks realized by a processor executing a program stored in the storage unit 13, an acquisition unit 121, a comparison unit 122, a determination unit 123, a battery stock acquisition unit 124, and a notification unit 125.

The storage unit 13 stores reservation information 131, return information 132, and station stock information 133, described below.

#### 2.1 Acquisition Unit

The acquisition unit 121 acquires, from each battery exchange station 20 and/or from user terminals 30, reservation information 131 indicating the number of batteries reserved by users for exchange at a given battery exchange station 20 within a predetermined period (hereinafter, "target period"), and return information 132 indicating the number of batteries expected to be returned to that battery exchange station 20 within the target period.

The target period may be defined, for example, as a time slot of a predetermined length (e.g., 30 minutes or 1 hour) into which each day is divided, or as a rolling window beginning at the current time and extending a predetermined duration into the future.

The reservation information 131 includes, for each existing reservation, an identifier of the reserved battery exchange station 20, a scheduled exchange time, a number of batteries requested, and a user identifier. The reservation information 131 is updated each time a new reservation is accepted or an existing reservation is cancelled.

The return information 132 is generated by one or a combination of the following methods:

(a) **Reported Scheduled Return**: When a user makes a reservation for a battery exchange at a certain time, the vehicle from which the depleted battery is being returned is treated as a "returning vehicle," and information regarding this vehicle's expected arrival time is registered as return information 132 for the corresponding battery exchange station 20.

(b) **Statistical Estimation**: The acquisition unit 121 refers to historical usage data classified by day of the week and time zone, stored in the storage unit 13, and calculates a statistically expected number of batteries to be returned within the target period, using a predetermined estimation model (for example, a moving average or a regression model).

(c) **Vehicle State Communication**: The acquisition unit 121 communicates with a vehicle-mounted communication device or a user terminal 30 of a user who is scheduled to visit a battery exchange station 20, and acquires a remaining charge level and a current position of the vehicle. Based on this information, the acquisition unit 121 estimates whether the vehicle is expected to arrive at the battery exchange station 20 within the target period and to return a depleted battery.

The return information 132 generated by methods (a) through (c) may be combined, for example by giving priority to reported information under method (a), supplementing missing data with the estimation of method (c), and using the statistical estimation of method (b) as a fallback when neither (a) nor (c) is available.

#### 2.2 Comparison Unit

The comparison unit 122 compares the number of reserved batteries (obtained from reservation information 131) with the number of returned batteries (obtained from return information 132), for the target period associated with a new reservation request. Specifically, in one embodiment, the comparison unit 122 calculates a difference value D, given by:

**D = (Number of Returned Batteries) − (Number of Reserved Batteries) − (Number of Batteries Requested in New Reservation)**

#### 2.3 Battery Stock Acquisition Unit

The battery stock acquisition unit 124 acquires, from the station control unit 24 of the relevant battery exchange station 20, a current stock number S indicating the number of charged batteries currently available for immediate exchange at that station, as station stock information 133.

#### 2.4 Determination Unit

The determination unit 123 determines whether the new reservation request can be accepted, based on the result of the comparison performed by the comparison unit 122, and optionally, the current stock number S acquired by the battery stock acquisition unit 124.

In a first embodiment, the determination unit 123 determines that the new reservation request can be accepted when the difference value D is equal to or greater than zero, and determines that the new reservation request cannot be accepted when the difference value D
